episodes.title: Week 9 Trench & Scheme Preview: Bosa + Buckner Debut vs. Klint Kubiak's Raiders
episodes.topic: Week 9 LV @ SF Matchup (SF -9.5), Raheem Morris Stunt Geometry & Maxx Crosby Protection Plan

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Welcome in to 49ers Faithful. Elena, it feels like we've been circling this Sunday at Levi's Stadium for a month. The 6-1 Niners come out of the Week 8 bye holding the #1 seed in the NFC, and Nick Bosa is officially off the injury report—cleared to hunt next to DeForest Buckner for the very first time.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Yeah, and the betting market noticed immediately. San Francisco opened at Opened SF -8.5 (Draft Kings) and steamed to SF -9.5 with a 51.5 total against the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders. Think about the protection math Raheem Morris can throw at offenses now.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Walk through that front-four geometry for a second. Because from Weeks 3 through 7 without Bosa, Osa Odighizuwa basically carried our interior pass rush on his back.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Right, and he was terrific doing it. Now Morris drops six-foot-seven DeForest Buckner into the 3-technique weak, shades Odighizuwa at the 2i strong, and puts Bosa and Keion White out on the Wide-9 rails. If Vegas slides the center toward Bosa, Buckner gets singled up on a guard. You just can't block both.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Exactly. And look across the sideline at who's calling plays for Las Vegas. First-year head coach Klint Kubiak spent all of 2023 right here in Santa Clara as Kyle Shanahan's Passing Game Specialist.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: So there are zero secrets on the tendencies tape.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: None at all. Kubiak wants outside zone with Ashton Jeanty to set up deep play-action crossers for Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers. That's the exact intermediate route spacing Fred Warner and Deommodore Lenoir bait with disguised split-safety rotations every single day in practice.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Plus we've got a full seven-day rest edge coming off the bye. Under Shanahan, when QB1 is healthy post-bye, the Niners average +0.21 EPA/play on their opening fifteen scripted snaps. And Brock Purdy has been surgical—+63.2 passing EPA, +4.3% CPOE, and just a 3.2% sack rate.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: The one guy who can wreck the script is Maxx Crosby. Whenever he flips away from Trent Williams to line up over Colton McKivitz at right tackle, expect heavy 21-personnel chip-and-release help from George Kittle and Kyle Juszczyk—plus quick rhythm throws to Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and Demarcus Robinson back off IR.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Keep Crosby off Purdy's spot on third-and-medium, keep Bosa on a smart 45-snap pitch count in his first game back, and that implied projection of SF 30.5 – LV 21.0 feels right on the money.

episodes.title: 2026–2028 Salary Cap Blueprint: Why $35.16M Must Roll Into 2027's -$31.54M Horizon
episodes.topic: OverTheCap Multi-Year Ledger, CBA Article 13 Rollover Bridge & Brandon Aiyuk Post-June 1 Mechanics

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Let's clear up the single biggest misconception floating around Niners Twitter this week, Marcus. People look at OverTheCap, see $35.16M in 2026 cap space, and treat it like free spending cash.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Yeah—until you click one tab forward to 2027. Connect those two ledgers for everyone.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: The moment you flip to 2027, San Francisco sits -$31.54M in the red against an estimated $327M cap ceiling. Under Article 13 of the CBA, every unused dollar from 2026 rolls over one-for-one into next spring.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: So that surplus isn't extra money—it's already spoken for.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: 100 percent. Brock Purdy's cap hit is $23.71M right now, and Nick Bosa sits at $22.99M, right before both deals jump sharply in 2027. If John Lynch and Paraag Marathe roll roughly $28M to $31M forward, they wipe out almost that entire 2027 deficit without kicking dead money down the road on older veterans.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Okay, so how does Brandon Aiyuk factor into that math? He met with team brass at SAP Performance Facility looking for reinstatement so both sides can map out an offseason exit.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Because we're past June first, any trade or release right now automatically uses Post-June-1 accounting. Only this season's bonus proration stays on the 2026 books, while the rest of his unamortized signing and option bonus accelerates onto 2027.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Which means a clean settlement on unaccrued guarantees is huge—otherwise an Aiyuk exit piles right on top of next year's crunch.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Exactly. And that's why hitting on cost-controlled rookie deals—Mykel Williams, Upton Stout, Renardo Green, Dominick Puni, Gracen Halton, and Romello Height—isn't just a nice bonus. It's the structural engine keeping this title window wide open.

episodes.title: Nov 10 Trade Window & Calibrated 34.5% NFC #1 Seed Outlook
episodes.topic: Ranked Positional Needs, 9/18ths Rental Purchasing Power, 6-Pick 2027 Draft Ledger & Empirical-Bayes Playoff Odds

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: We're inside the final countdown to Tuesday's November 10th, 1 PM Pacific trade deadline. John Lynch already sent our 2027 fourth-rounder to Indy to bring DeForest Buckner home. Looking strictly at the film and the injury wire, Elena, how do you stack our remaining needs?

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Number one is perimeter receiver or a 12-personnel move tight end. With six wideouts on reserve or sidelined lists, rookie-contract separators like Adonai Mitchell on the Jets, Josh Downs in Indy, Rashod Bateman in Baltimore, or Greg Dulcich from Miami make a ton of sense.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: And right behind receiver, it's got to be left guard pass protection next to Trent Williams, plus a true speed edge rusher.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Spot on. Someone like Kingsley Suamataia on a rookie deal at guard, or Khalil Mack from the 0-7 Chargers as a pure expiring one-year pass-rush rental—with Donte Jackson in that same Chargers boat if you want dime corner speed.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Let's clear up the cap mechanics on a guy like Mack, though. With 9/18ths of the season left, do the Niners actually need a seller to eat salary?

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Not at all—and getting that direction right really matters. Signing bonus proration stays with the seller, and the buyer only takes on 9/18ths of remaining 2026 base pay. So our $35.16M in 2026 space is actually worth over $65M+ in annualized base-salary buying power right now.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: So the bottleneck isn't 2026 cash—it's next year's -$31.54M cap horizon and having only 6 total picks left in the 2027 draft.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Bingo. That's why you target cheap rookie contracts or true expiring rentals for Day-3 picks, and steer way clear of zero-sack age-37 traps like Cameron Jordan or pricey extended starters like Michael Mayer.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Tie that back to our 10,000-run NFC playoff simulator before we wrap—because raw un-regressed models always overhype early 6-1 starts.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Right. Once you blend Empirical-Bayes regressed team power with net EPA, strength of schedule, and NFL tiebreakers, the 6-1 Niners project for 12 wins. That's a 93% playoff berth, 82.6% to take the NFC West, and a calibrated 34.5% shot at the #1 seed bye—just ahead of 6-1 Minnesota at 29.6% and 6-2 Chicago at 15.1%. Circle Week 11 against Minnesota in Mexico City—that's the swing game for the whole conference.

sharedAnalyses.title: 2026 Trade Window & Calibrated 10,000-Run Playoff Blueprint: Ranked Needs, Rental Math, -$31.54M 2027 Cap Horizon & 34.5% #1 Bye Odds
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### 1. Midseason CBA Purchasing Power vs. 2027 Cap & Draft Reality
* **9/18ths Proration Purchasing Power**: Acquiring teams absorb only the remaining **9/18ths** of a player's 2026 base salary while signing/option bonus proration stays on the seller's cap. With **`$35.16M`** in 2026 Top-51 space, San Francisco holds **>`$65M` in annualized base-salary purchasing power** and does **not** need sellers to eat 2026 salary.
* **The True Front-Office Constraints**:
  1. **`-$31.54M` Projected 2027 Cap Deficit** (on an estimated `$327.0M` ceiling): Every 2026 dollar spent reduces 1-for-1 CBA Article 13 rollover needed for 2027 compliance.
  2. **6 Total 2027 Draft Picks**: After trading SF's own 2027 4th-rounder to Indianapolis for **DeForest Buckner**, San Francisco owns **Rd 1 (#31), Rd 2 (#63), Rd 3 (#95), Rd 5 (#170), Rd 6 (#193 via BAL), and Rd 7 (#245 via KC)**—leaving a 75-pick gap between #95 and #170.

### 2. Verified Ranked Needs, Targets & Traps to Avoid
1. **Perimeter WR / 12-Personnel Move TE (Critical)**: With Ricky Pearsall (Season-Ending IR), Christian Kirk (IR — Meniscus), and De'Zhaun Stribling (IR — Ankle) on Injured Reserve, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. ruled Out on the active roster, and Brandon Aiyuk on Reserve/Left Squad, top cost-controlled fits are **Adonai Mitchell** (NYJ, `~$0.79M` prorated), **Josh Downs** (IND, `~$1.72M`), **Rashod Bateman** (BAL), and **Greg Dulcich** (MIA, `~$0.60M` expiring). *Note on **Quentin Johnston** (LAC): viable only if LAC restructures/retains his guaranteed `$18.0M` 2027 5th-year option.*
2. **Left Guard Pass Protection (High)**: Upgrade interior anchor next to **Trent Williams** via rookie-scale **Kingsley Suamataia** (KC, `~$0.65M` prorated).
3. **Rotational Speed EDGE & Dime DB (Targeted Rentals)**: Expiring one-year rentals on 0-7 LAC—**Khalil Mack** (`$4.0M` prorated, `$0` in 2027) and **Donte Jackson** (`$3.0M` prorated)—or **Jessie Bates III** (ATL, played under DC **Raheem Morris** in 2024–2025, contract voids after 2026).
* **Traps to Reject**: Zero-sack age-37 edge **Cameron Jordan** (0.0 sacks in 7 games), recently extended **Michael Mayer** (LV 3-yr/`$45M` deal), and burning Day-2 picks (#63/#95) on contender starters.

### 3. Calibrated 10,000-Run Playoff Probabilities (Why SF Sits at `34.5%` for the #1 Bye)
* **Empirical-Bayes + Net EPA + SOS Calibration**: Shrinking 7-game sample variance toward league priors (`gp / (gp + 9.5)`) with per-game posterior uncertainty and full NFL Section 16 multi-club tiebreakers places the **6-1** 49ers at **`12` projected wins**, **`93%` Playoff Berth**, **`82.6%` NFC West Title**, and **`34.5%` #1 Seed First-Round Bye**—leading **Minnesota (`6-1`, `29.6%`)** and **Chicago (`6-2`, `15.1%`)** entering the pivotal Week 11 neutral-site H2H clash vs. Minnesota in Mexico City.

sharedAnalyses.title: Scheme & EPA Deep Dive: How DC Raheem Morris, DeForest Buckner & Osa Odighizuwa Transform Nick Bosa’s Pass-Rush Geometry
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### Executive Finding
Under Defensive Coordinator **Raheem Morris**, pairing **DeForest Buckner** (6'7", 295 lbs, 34.4" arm length) and **Osa Odighizuwa** inside with **Nick Bosa** and **Keion White** on the Wide-9 rails eliminates the #1 protection adjustment offenses used against San Francisco in 2024–2025: **5-man half-slide + RB chip toward Bosa**.

### Key Quantitative & Film Mechanics
1. **Interior Slide Conflict (2i / 3-Tech Split)**:
   * When Morris aligns Buckner at the 3-technique weak and Odighizuwa at the 2i/shade strong, the opposing center must turn toward Odighizuwa or risk immediate A-gap penetration in the quarterback's lap (2.4s pocket collapse).
   * If the center slides away from Buckner + Bosa's side, the offensive guard is left on an island against Buckner's forklift bull-rush, preventing the guard from widening to help the tackle on **T-E (Tackle-End) stunts**.
2. **Early-Down Run-Fit Integrity & Disguised Split-Safety Rotations**:
   * Through Week 7 without Bosa for 5 games, SF relied heavily on **Fred Warner** erasing leaky B-gap creases. Buckner's career tackle-for-loss rate against outside zone restores two-gap knock-back, letting Morris spin two-high shells into late Cover-3 Buzz and Quarters robbers behind a dominant 4-man rush.
3. **Snap-Count Pitch Count Projection (Week 9 vs. Raiders)**:
   * Expect Bosa around **42–46 snaps (~68%)**, with **Mykel Williams**, **Keion White**, and 3rd-round rookie **Romello Height** rotating on early run downs and 2nd-and-long speed rushes.

sharedAnalyses.title: Brock Purdy 2026 Through 7 Games: Why +4.25% CPOE & 3.2% Sack Avoidance Sustain Top-3 NFL Offense
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### 2026 Statistical Snapshot (6-1 Record)
* **Passing Efficiency**: `146/211 (69.2%)`, `1,748 Yards (8.28 YPA)`, `15 TD`, `4 INT`
* **Total Passing EPA**: `+63.23` (plus `+14.38` rushing EPA on `161` scramble/zone-read yards)
* **Completion % Over Expected (CPOE)**: `+4.25%`
* **Sacks Taken**: Only `7 sacks` across `218 dropbacks` (`3.2% sack rate`)

### What Changed on Film in 2026
1. **Faster Backside Checkdowns vs. Simulated Pressures**: Rather than hunting low-percentage hero throws when two-high shells bracket the deep over route, Purdy has slashed his pressure-to-sack conversion by hitting **Christian McCaffrey** and **George Kittle** on hot option/angle outlets within `3s`.
2. **Anticipation Window Between the Numbers (10–19 Air Yards)**: Even with Brandon Aiyuk on Reserve/Left Squad, Ricky Pearsall on season-ending IR since August, Christian Kirk on IR, and veteran wideouts Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. missing time, Purdy has sustained elite intermediate efficiency (`85` passing first downs) by trusting **Brandin Cooks**, **Jordan Watkins**, and **Jacob Cowing** before they clear linebacker leverage.
